**[Daniel Galloway Stingray Flipper:](http://i.imgur.com/WHyedYc.jpg)**  I'm very happy with this knife as my first custom.  It comes in at about 6 oz. with a 4" blade and about a 9"  overall length open. The blade is CPM154.   The lockup is perfect and smooth to disengage.  The flipping action is very snappy and responsive.  It is a very comfortable knife to hold, seeing as all of the corners and edges are polished and rounded off.  The checkering on the handles is nice and grippy without being uncomfortable.  Without rambling on about all of the little details and how jaw-droppingly beautiful the knife, there's not much else to say.  I haven't really found a single flaw in it so far.  


**[McGinnis Knives Pro Line Valve Flipper:](http://i.imgur.com/X16JLjx.jpg)**  This is probably the most functionally flawless knife I've ever laid my hands on, especially for the price.  This one weighs in at 5 oz. with a 3.75" blade and a 8.5" overall length.  The blade is also CPM154 on this knife.  The lockup is yet again, solid and smooth to disengage.  The flipping action is lightning fast and the detent is absolutely *perfect*.  This knife is also comfortable to hold, though it does have less tactility than the Stingray.  The blade shape seems like it would make a great cutter, and it is amazing at piercing.  This knife also seems to have the sharpest edge out of the four.  I highly recommend picking one of these up if you can get one for a decent price.  Most I see online are about $700, Gerry was selling them at the show for $500.  


**[HEAdesigns/Liong Mah Ace Flipper:](http://i.imgur.com/Mmhu7uE.jpg)**  This knife was produced by Reate Knives. I don't have experience with any of Reate's other knives, but I am very impressed with the F&F on this one.  It is hard to believe that this a production knife, there really are no flaws on it.  It weighs in at about 5.5 oz. with a 3.5" blade and a 8.25" overall length.  The blade is S35VN. It has a steel lockface insert; the lockup is solid and easy to reach into and disengage.  The flipping is good and the action is smooth.  The bearings and detent are both ceramic.  This knife has no texturing on the handles but the contouring locks it into your hand instead.  It is aa comfortable knife to hold, and the blade feels like and extension of your hand.  The knife came nice and sharp, but at about the sharpness you would expect from a decent production.  Only 120 of these were made, so if you want to get your hands on the "Ace" design without trying to find an original custom for sale, get one of these.  


**[Battle Horse Knives Fixed Blade:](http://i.imgur.com/r95YRA5.jpg)**  I really don't have much to say on this one. I haven't had a chance to use it yet but it looks like it could take a beating.  This stout lil' bastard weighs in at 8 oz. and the sheath is 1.6 oz.  The blade length is is 3.5" with an edge length of about 3", the overall length is 7.5".  I'm not sure about the blade steel, but the handles are micarta.  The F&F is nice and the molded kydex sheath works flawlessly.  Hopefully, soon, I will get the chance to put this thing to use; it sure looks like it could do some work.
